declaration: fix-declaration.json, committed before any fix code (tag fix-before)
outcome: Gate did NOT move. Rooms with at least one dimension: 0 of 1 before, 0 of 1 after, on all three runs.

runs.finding: Derived stills were rotated 90 degrees; Stray logs the sensor in landscape orientation.
After rotating stills upright from logged gravity (what an EXIF tag does on a real iPhone), none of the 7 stills of single_room shows floor and ceiling together.
Same on single_scan_with_ceiling, whose LiDAR run gives a 2.33 m ceiling: each still shows the ceiling or the floor, not both.

prediction_check: The declared conditional branch held (0 of 1 if no still shows floor and ceiling together). The success criterion (1 of 1) was not met.
root_cause_verdict: Half right. SfM does fail on sparse stills and the pipeline did discard usable per-image depth. But a single view yields a dimension only when floor and ceiling share the frame, and the derived stills (close-range, tilted, narrow field of view) rarely do. The missing ingredient is cross-view scale or gravity, not just a fallback.
what_shipped: Single-view fallback (precision over recall: no value if floor and ceiling planes are not both found and parallel), upright derivation, rectangle layout default, damage opt-in.
not_claimed: No accuracy movement and no photo-tier gate pass. Intervals remain uncalibrated; no physical ground truth.
protocol_change_from_finding: CAPTURE_PROTOCOL.txt now asks for one level wide shot per room from a doorway showing floor and ceiling together.
next: Estimate camera height and gravity from several views (cross-view planes) or require a wide shot, then re-declare before changing code.
